As for one who offers another food containing poison, he has treated him gently in the moment, since he did not make him swallow pure poison but concealed it in sweetness; so it is not far-fetched to say, "he has bestowed a favor upon him." If this is established, then blessings are of two kinds: blessings of benefit and blessings of repelling. The blessings of benefit are what reaches them of kinds of pleasures, and the blessings of repelling are what is turned away from them of kinds of calamities. On this basis Allah has bestowed upon the disbelievers blessings of repelling, by unanimous agreement, namely what is averted from them of pains and illnesses, and there is no disagreement among them that He did not bestow upon them the blessing of His religion. And praise is to Allah.

The nineteenth point concerns His words: ﴿But those who fear their Lord﴾. It is an exception (istidrak) after a statement that carried the sense of negation, because the meaning of what came before is that they have no great benefit from their movement in the lands, but for the God-fearing there is great benefit and eternal abiding. So the position of "lakin" is nominative by inception. Yazid ibn al-Qa'qa' read "lakinna" with the nun doubled.

The twentieth point concerns His words: ﴿A welcome gift from Allah﴾. Nuzulan is like thawaban according to the Basrans; according to al-Kisa'i it is a verbal noun. Al-Farra' said: it is an explanatory element. Al-Hasan and al-Nakha'i read "nuzulan" with the zay lightened, finding two dammas burdensome; the rest read it with the zay heavy. The nuzul is what is prepared for the guest, and the nazil is the guest. The poet said:

The guest of a people is the greatest of them in rights, and the right of Allah is in the right of the guest.

The plural is al-anzal. "Hazzun nazil" means gathered. Nuzul (with dhamma then sukun, or with fatha) also means the surplus, and one says "food of nuzul and nuzl."

The twenty-first point: I say, perhaps the nuzul, and Allah knows best, is what came in the Sahih of Muslim from the hadith of Thawban, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in the story of the rabbi who asked the Prophet ﷺ: "Where will people be on the day the earth is changed to other than the earth and the heavens?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "They will be in darkness beyond the bridge." He said: "Who among the people will cross first?" He said: "The poor among the emigrants." The Jew said: "What is their gift (tuhfah) when they enter Paradise?" He said: "The extra piece of the liver of the fish (ziyadat kabid al-nun)." He said: "What is their food after it?" He said: "The bull of Paradise will be slaughtered for them, which used to graze on its outskirts." He said: "What is their drink with it?" He said: "From a spring in it called Salsabil," and he mentioned the hadith. The lexicographers said: the tuhfah is what a person is presented with of fruits, and the tarf is its finest and most delicate things, and this matches what we mentioned concerning the nuzul. And Allah knows best. Ziyadat al-kabid is a piece of it like a finger. Al-Harawi said: "A welcome gift from Allah," meaning a reward; it was also said, provision.

﴿And what is with Allah is better for the righteous﴾, meaning better than what the disbelievers enjoy in this world. And Allah knows best.

The twenty-second point concerns His words: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Book are those who believe in Allah﴾, the verse. Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, Anas, Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah and al-Hasan said: it was revealed concerning the Negus, because when he died Jibril, peace be upon him, informed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of his death, and the Prophet ﷺ said to his companions: "Stand and pray over your brother the Negus." Some of them said to others: "He orders us to pray over a non-Arab, one of the uncouth Abyssinians." So Allah revealed: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Book are those who believe in Allah and in what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them.﴾ Al-Dahhak said: "what has been revealed to you" is the Qur'an.

﴿And what has been revealed to them﴾ is the Torah and the Gospel. In the Revelation: ﴿Those will be given their reward twice﴾ [al-Qasas: 54] [[See vol. 13, p. 297.]]. In the Sahih of Muslim: "Three will be given their reward twice," and he mentioned them, including "a man of the People of the Book who believed in his prophet, then encountered the Prophet ﷺ, believed in him, followed him and affirmed him; he has two rewards," and he related the hadith. Prayer over him and what scholars hold regarding prayer over an absent deceased have already been discussed in al-Baqarah, so there is no point in repeating it. Mujahid, Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd said: it was revealed concerning believers among the People of the Book, and this is general, and the Negus is one of them. His name was Ashamah, which in Arabic is 'Ata'ah (gift). And ﴿humble﴾ means lowly, and it is accusative as a circumstantial state (hal) of the pronoun in "yu'minu." It was also said: it is a state of the pronoun in "ilayhim" or "ilaykum." What is in the verse is clear, and it has already been discussed.

The twenty-third point concerns His words: ﴿O you who believe, persevere﴾, the verse. Allah concluded the sura with what this tenth verse includes of the admonitions that gather victory in this world over enemies and success with the bliss of the Hereafter. He urged patience in obedience and restraint from desires. Patience is restraint, and its explanation has already been given in al-Baqarah [[See vol. 2, p. 174.]]. He commanded mutual steadfastness (musabarah), and it was said its meaning is steadfastness against enemies; this was said by Zayd ibn Aslam.

Al-Hasan said: "[It means] the five daily prayers." It was also said: "[It means] persistent opposition to the self in its desires, for it calls to them while he restrains it."

ʿAtaʾ and al-Qurazi said: "Be patient in the face of the promise that was made to you," i.e., do not despair, and await relief. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Waiting for relief with patience is an act of worship." Abu ʿUmar (Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr), may Allah have mercy on him, preferred this view. The first view is the view of the majority, and from it is the verse of ʿAntarah:

"I have not seen living people who endure as we endure,
nor who confront as those we confront."

His words "endure as we endure" mean: they endured the enemy in war, and no cowardice or weakness appeared from them. "Mukafahah" means facing and confronting one another in battle. For this reason they differed concerning the meaning of His words (wa-rabitu) ["and be steadfast in readiness"]. The majority of the community said: "Be steadfast in readiness against your enemies with horses," i.e., tie up horses as your enemies tie them up. From it is the words of the Most High: ﴿And of steeds held in readiness﴾ [al-Anfal: 60] [[See vol. 8, p. 36.]]

In the Muwatta' of Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: Abu ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrah wrote to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab mentioning the armies of the Romans and what he feared from them. ʿUmar wrote to him: "To proceed: whatever hardship befalls a believing servant, Allah will make relief after it, and indeed one hardship will never overcome two eases. Allah the Most High says in His Book: ﴿O you who believe, be patient, endure in patience, be steadfast in readiness, and fear Allah that you may be successful﴾."

Abu Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman said: this verse concerns waiting for prayer after prayer, and there was no campaign in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in which one stayed in readiness. Al-Hakim Abu ʿAbd Allah related it in his Sahih. Abu Salamah cited his (peace be upon him) saying: "Shall I not direct you to that by which Allah erases sins and raises ranks? Performing ablution thoroughly despite hardship, walking many steps to the mosques, and waiting for prayer after prayer—that is steadfastness in readiness" (repeated three times). Related by Malik.

Ibn ʿAtiyyah said: The correct view is that ribat [here, "ribat" is from the manuscripts B, J, H, and T] is constant attachment in the way of Allah. Its origin is from tying horses, then every one constantly stationed at a frontier of the frontiers of Islam [in B: "the Muslims"] was called murabit, whether mounted or on foot. The term is derived from rabt (tying). The saying of the Prophet ﷺ "that is ribat" is only a figurative comparison to ribat in the way of Allah. The lexical ribat is the first meaning, and this is [in B: "thus"] like his saying: "The strong man is not the one who overthrows others" [sur'ah, one who is never defeated in wrestling], and his saying: "The poor man is not this wanderer," and so on.

I say: His words "The lexical ribat is the first meaning" are not accepted, for al-Khalil ibn Ahmad, one of the imams and trustworthy authorities of the language, said: ribat is constant presence at the frontiers, and also persistence in prayer. Thus waiting for prayer is literally ribat, as the Prophet ﷺ said. More than this is what al-Shaybani said: it is said "maʾ mutarabit," i.e., water that is perpetual and never drawn off. Ibn Faris related it, and this requires extending the lexical meaning of ribat beyond what we have mentioned. For among the Arabs, murabatah is binding a thing firmly so that it does not come loose and return to what one has been patient about, thus holding the heart to good intention and the body to obedience. Among its greatest and most important forms is tying horses in the way of Allah, as explicitly stated in revelation in His words: ﴿And of steeds held in readiness﴾ [al-Anfal: 60], as will come. Binding the self to the prayers is as the Prophet ﷺ said, related by Abu Hurayrah, Jabir and ʿAli, and "there is no perfume after a bride."

Twenty-fourth issue: The one stationed in the way of Allah, according to the jurists, is the one who travels to a frontier to remain there for a period of time, as said by Muhammad ibn al-Mawwaz [and he related it]. As for the permanent residents of the frontiers with their families, who build and earn their living there, although they are protectors they are not stationed (murabitun). Ibn ʿAtiyyah said: Ibn Khuwayz Mindad said: ribat has two states: a state in which the frontier is secure and impregnable, where it is permissible to settle there with family and children; and if it is not secure, it is permissible for one who is fit for fighting to station himself there personally, but he should not bring family and children there, lest the enemy prevail, take captives and enslave them. And Allah knows best.

Twenty-fifth issue: Many hadiths have come concerning the merit of ribat, among them what al-Bukhari related from Sahl ibn Saʿd al-Saʿidi that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A day of ribat in the way of Allah is better with Allah than the world and all that is in it." And in Sahih Muslim, from Salman, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "A day and a night of ribat is better than a month of fasting and standing in prayer by night for it, and if he dies, his deeds which he used to do continue for him, his provision is continued for him, and he is safe from the tempter." [[al-Fattan: the Devil. It is related with a fatha and with a damma on the fa. Whoever reads it with fatha means a single one, because he tempts people away from religion. Whoever reads it with damma means the plural of fatin, i.e., they assist one another in misleading people from the truth and tempting them.]] Abu Dawud related in his Sunan from Fadalah ibn ʿUbayd that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Every dead person has his deeds sealed except the one stationed (murabit), for his deed continues to grow for him until the Day of Resurrection, and he is safe from the tormentor of the grave."

In these two hadiths there is evidence that ribat is the best of the deeds whose reward remains after death, as came in the hadith of al-ʿAla' ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "When a person dies, his deeds are cut off except from three: ongoing charity, knowledge from which benefit is gained, or a righteous child who prays for him." [[This is the narration of Muslim as in the Kitab al-Wasiyyah. Likewise in Z, T, Ha, J. In another narration: "Ibn Adam." The hadith was related by al-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i with the wording: "except from three: charity..." and al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad.]] It is a sound hadith, related by Muslim alone. The ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge and righteous child who prays for his parents are cut off by the exhaustion of charities, the passing of knowledge and the death of the child. But the reward of ribat is multiplied until the Day of Resurrection, for growth has no meaning except multiplication, and this is not conditional upon a cause that would be cut off when it ends; rather it is a perpetual bounty from Allah the Most High until the Day of Resurrection. This is because all acts of righteousness can only be undertaken with safety from the enemy and guarding against it, by protecting the core of religion and upholding the symbols of Islam. The deed whose reward continues is what he used to do of righteous deeds. Ibn Majah related with a sound chain from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Whoever dies while stationed in the way of Allah, the reward of the righteous deed he used to do continues for him, his provision continues for him, he is safe from the tempter, and Allah will raise him on the Day of Resurrection secure from terror." In this hadith there is a second condition, which is death in the state of ribat. And Allah knows best.

It is related from ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Whoever stations himself for one night in the way of Allah, it is for him like a thousand nights of fasting and standing in prayer."

It is related from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, a day of ribat in the way of Allah, guarding the weak point of the Muslims, seeking reward, other than in Ramadan, is greater in reward than a hundred years of worship, fasting and standing in prayer. And a day of ribat in the way of Allah, guarding the weak point of the Muslims, seeking reward, in Ramadan, is better with Allah and greater in reward—I think he said: than a thousand years of worship, fasting and standing in prayer. If Allah returns him safe to his family, no sin is recorded against him for a thousand years, and good deeds are recorded for him, and the reward of ribat continues for him until the Day of Resurrection." [[The narration of Ibn Majah.]]

This hadith indicates that a day of ribat in Ramadan obtains lasting reward even if one does not die while stationed.

And Allah knows best. It is related from Anas ibn Malik who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Guarding one night in the way of Allah is better than a man's fasting and standing in prayer with his family for a thousand years; the year is three hundred and sixty days, and the day is like a thousand years." [[In J.]]

I say: It has also come concerning waiting for prayer after prayer that it is ribat, so the one who awaits the prayers may attain that merit, if Allah the Most High wills. Abu Nuʿaym al-Hafiz related: Sulayman ibn Ahmad told us, ʿAli ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz told us, Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal told us [ḥ — the transition mark used by hadith scholars when a hadith has two or more chains, read as "al-hadith" by the reciter, as explained in the note]; and Abu Bakr ibn Malik told us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal told us, my father told me, al-Hasan ibn Musa told me, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Abu Ayyub al-Azdi, from Nawf al-Bikali, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, that the Prophet ﷺ prayed Maghrib one night and we prayed with him. Some people remained for supererogatory prayer and some went home. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came before the people had turned to the ʿIsha' prayer, and came while the people were present, raising his finger, having counted twenty-nine, pointing with the index finger to the sky. He drew up his garment from his knees and said: "Rejoice, assembly of Muslims! This is your Lord who has opened a gate of the gates of heaven, boasting of you to the angels, saying: O My angels, look at these servants of Mine, who have completed an obligatory prayer while awaiting another."

Hammad ibn Salamah related it from ʿAli ibn Zayd from Mutarrif ibn ʿAbd Allah: that Nawf and ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr met, and Nawf related from the Torah, and ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr related this hadith from the Prophet ﷺ.

(And fear Allah) i.e., you were not commanded to fight without taqwa.

(That you may be successful) so that you may be hopeful of success. It was also said: la'alla means li-kay (in order that). Al-falah is endurance (baqa'). All of this has passed in al-Baqarah in full detail [[See vol. 1, pp. 162, 182, 227.]], and praise be to Allah.

The commentary on Surah Al ʿImran has been completed from (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran wa-l-Mubayyin lima Tadammana min al-Sunnah wa-Ayi al-Furqan), by the grace and help of Allah.

Verified by Abu Ishaq Ibrahim al-Tafayyash.

The fourth part of the Tafsir of al-Qurtubi is complete, followed, God willing, by the fifth part. Surah al-Nisa' — by Allah's help and gracious guidance. The fourth part of the book (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) of al-Qurtubi, fifth part, has been printed.

**Question 1:** There are twenty-five issues in this passage. The first is the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾. The meaning of this verse has already been discussed in *al-Baqarah* (see vol. 2, p. 191) and in other places. Allah concluded this surah by commanding contemplation and reasoning about His signs, since these signs can only proceed from a Living, Self-Subsisting, All-Powerful, Holy, Peaceful One who is free of need from the worlds, so that their faith may rest on certainty and not on mere imitation (taqlid).

﴿Are signs for those of understanding﴾: those who use their minds to reflect on the proofs. It is narrated from ʿAishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: When this verse was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ, he stood to pray. Bilal came to inform him of the prayer and saw him weeping. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, do you weep when Allah has forgiven you your earlier and later sins?" He said: "O Bilal, should I not be a grateful servant? Allah has revealed to me tonight a verse: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, are signs for those of understanding﴾." Then he said: "Woe to the one who recites it and does not reflect upon it."

**Question 2:** The scholars said: It is recommended for one who wakes from sleep to wipe his face and to begin his night prayer by reciting these ten verses, following the example of the Prophet ﷺ. This is established in the *Sahihayn* (al-Bukhari and Muslim) and elsewhere, and it will come. Then he prays what has been decreed for him. Thus he combines reflection and action, and this is the best of deeds [17 line deleted in the manuscript] whose explanation will come in this verse after this.

It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite ten verses from the end of *Al ʿImran* every night. Abu Nasr al-Wa'ili al-Sijistani, the hafiz, recorded it in his book *al-Ibanah* from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Musa, from Muzahir ibn Aslam al-Makhzumi, from al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurairah. The beginning of the surah has already been discussed (see p. 2 of this part) regarding ʿUthman, who said: Whoever recites the end of *Al ʿImran* in a night, the reward of a night of prayer is written for him.

**Question 3:** The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Those who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides﴾. Allah mentioned three states in which the son of Adam does not usually fail to be, in most of his affairs, so these states seem to encompass his time. In this sense is the saying of ʿAishah, may Allah be pleased with her: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to remember Allah in all his states." It was recorded by Muslim. This includes his being in the toilet and other situations.

The scholars differed on this. ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr, Ibn Sirin, and al-Nakhaʿi permitted it, while Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAta', and al-Shaʿbi disliked it. The first view is more correct because of the generality of the verse and the hadith. Al-Nakhaʿi said: "There is no harm in remembering Allah in the toilet, for it rises," meaning: it rises (to Allah) with the angels, written in their scrolls, so the word "it" is an omitted noun (the remembrance). The evidence is the words of Allah: ﴿Not a word does he utter but that with him is an observer, ready﴾ [Qaf: 18], and His words: ﴿And indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording﴾ [al-Infitar: 10–11]. Also, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded His servants to remember Him in every state without exception, saying: ﴿Remember Allah with much remembrance﴾ [al-Ahzab: 41], and: ﴿So remember Me; I will remember you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 152], and: ﴿Indeed, We do not allow the reward of those who do good to be lost﴾ [al-Kahf: 30]. Thus the command is general. So the one who remembers Allah in all his states is rewarded, if Allah wills.

Abu Nuʿaym reported: Abu Bakr ibn Malik narrated to us, ʿAbdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from ʿAta' ibn Abi Marwan, from his father, from Kaʿb al-Ahbar, who said: Musa, peace be upon him, said: "O Lord, are You near so that I may whisper to You, or far so that I may call out to You?" He said: "O Musa, I am the companion of the one who remembers Me." He said: "O Lord, we are in states in which we would honor You and glorify You by not remembering You." He said: "What are they?" He said: "Sexual impurity and defecation." He said: "O Musa, remember Me in every state."

The dislike of those who disliked it is either out of glorifying the remembrance of Allah in places where it is disliked to mention Him, like the dislike of reciting the Qur'an in the bathhouse, or out of sparing the noble recording angels from being placed in places of filth and impurity while writing what is uttered. And Allah knows best.

The phrase "standing and sitting" is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl).

﴿And on their sides﴾: in the position of a circumstantial clause, meaning: and lying down. A similar expression is the words of Allah: ﴿He calls Us, whether lying on his side or sitting or standing﴾ [Yunus: 12], in reverse order, meaning: He called Us while lying on his side.

A group of commentators, including al-Hasan and others, held that the words "they remember Allah" to the end refer to the prayer, meaning: they do not neglect it. In a state of excuse, they pray sitting or on their sides. This is like the words of Allah: ﴿So when you have finished the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides﴾ [al-Nisa': 103], according to the view of Ibn Masʿud, as will be explained. If the verse concerns prayer, its jurisprudence is that a person prays standing; if he cannot, then sitting; if he cannot, then on his side. This is as established from ʿImran ibn Husayn, who said: I had hemorrhoids, so I asked the Prophet ﷺ about prayer, and he said: "Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; if you cannot, then on your side." The imams related it. The Prophet ﷺ used to pray sitting in optional prayers a year before his death, as is in *Sahih Muslim*. Al-Nasa'i narrated from ʿAishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ praying cross-legged." Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman (al-Nasa'i's kunyah) said: "I know of no one who narrated this hadith except Abu Dawud al-Hafari (a nisbah to a place in Kufa; his name is ʿUmar ibn Saʿd ibn ʿUbayd), and he is trustworthy, but I do not think this hadith is anything but an error. And Allah knows best."

**Question 4:** The scholars differed on the manner and form of the prayer of the sick and of the one who sits. Ibn ʿAbd al-Hakam reported from Malik that he sits cross-legged while standing. Al-Buwayti reported from al-Shafiʿi: "When he wants to prostrate, he prepares himself for prostration according to what he can bear." He said: "The same applies to one praying an optional prayer." Similar is the view of al-Thawri. Likewise said al-Layth, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad. Al-Shafiʿi in the narration of al-Muzani said: He sits throughout his entire prayer as one sits for the tashahhud. This was also reported from Malik and his companions, but the first, which is well-known (in the school, al-madhhab; this was corrected in the margin), is the apparent view of the *Mudawwanah*. Abu Hanifah and Zufar said: He sits as one sits for the tashahhud, and similarly he bows and prostrates (while sitting).

**Question 5:** He said: If he cannot sit, he prays on his side or his back, by choice. This is the position of the *Mudawwanah*. Ibn Habib related from Ibn al-Qasim: He prays on his back; if he cannot, then on his right side; then on his left side. In the book of Ibn al-Mawwaz it is the reverse: he prays on his right side, otherwise on his left, otherwise on his back. Sahnun said: He prays on his right side, as he is placed in his grave, otherwise on his back, otherwise on his left. Malik and Abu Hanifah said: When one prays lying down, his feet should be toward the qiblah. Al-Shafiʿi and al-Thawri said: He prays on his side with his face toward the qiblah.

**Question 6:** If he regains strength during the prayer because the illness has lessened, Ibn al-Qasim said: He stands for the rest of his prayer and builds on what has passed. This is also the view of al-Shafiʿi, Zufar, and al-Tabari. Abu Hanifah and his two companions, Yaʿqub and Muhammad, said regarding one who prayed one rak'ah lying down and then recovered: he must begin the prayer again from its beginning. But if he was praying sitting, bowing and prostrating, and then recovered, he builds upon it according to Abu Hanifah, and does not build upon it according to Muhammad. Abu Hanifah and his companions said: If one begins the prayer standing and then reaches the point of gesturing (iʾma'), he should continue building on it. This was narrated from Abu Yusuf. Malik said regarding the sick person who cannot bow or prostrate, but can stand and sit: he prays standing and gestures for bowing; when he wants to prostrate, he sits and gestures for prostration. This is also the view of Abu Yusuf and the analogy of al-Shafiʿi's view. Abu Hanifah and his companions said: He prays sitting.

**Question 7:** As for the prayer of the one who sleeps while healthy: there is an addition narrated in the hadith of ʿImran ibn Husayn that is not found elsewhere: "The prayer of the one who sleeps is like half the prayer of the one who sits." Abu ʿUmar said: The majority of scholars do not permit optional prayer while lying down. This hadith was not narrated except by Husayn al-Muʿallim, namely Husayn ibn Dhakwan, from ʿAbdullah ibn Buraydah, from ʿImran ibn Husayn. It has been disputed regarding its chain and its text in a way that requires caution about it. If it is authentic, I do not know its meaning. If any of the scholars permitted optional prayer lying down for one who is able to sit or stand, then its basis is this addition in the report, and it is the evidence for those who hold that view. But if they agreed on the dislike of optional prayer while lying down for one able to sit or stand, then the hadith of Husayn is either an error or abrogated.

It was also said: The meaning of the verse is those who infer from the creation of the heavens and the earth that what changes must have a changer, and that changer must be capable of perfection, and that He can send messengers. If He sends a messenger and shows the truth of his message by a single miracle, no one has an excuse. These are the ones who remember Allah in every state. And Allah knows best.

**Question 8:** The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And they reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾. We have already explained the meaning of "they remember," which is either remembrance by the tongue or prayer, obligatory and optional. Thus Allah joined another act of worship to one of them (in some manuscripts: "joined another worship, which is reflection"), namely reflection on the power of Allah and His creatures, and the lessons He scattered, so that this may increase their insight:

*And in everything there is a sign*
*indicating that He is one.*

Al-Qurtubi said: It has been said that "yatafakkarun" (they reflect) is coordinated (ʿatf) with the circumstantial clause (al-ḥāl). It has also been said that it is an independent clause (munqaṭiʿ), but the first view is closer to the meaning. Al-fikra (reflection) is the heart's repeated turning over of a matter. One says "tafakkara" (he reflected), and a man who is "fakīr" is one who reflects much. The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by a people who were reflecting about Allah, and he said: "Reflect on the creation, and do not reflect on the Creator, for you cannot measure His measure." Reflection, consideration, and the expansion of the mind over created things are what is meant, as He said: ﴿And they reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth.﴾

It is related that Sufyan al-Thawri (may Allah be pleased with him) prayed two rak'ahs behind the Maqam (the Station of Ibrahim). Then he raised his head to the sky, and when he saw the stars he fainted. He used to urinate blood because of his prolonged grief and reflection.

It is narrated from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "While a man was lying on his bed, he raised his head, looked at the stars and the sky, and said: 'I bear witness that You are a Lord and a Creator. O Allah, forgive me.' Then Allah looked at him and forgave him." He (ﷺ) also said: "There is no worship like reflection." And it is related from him (peace be upon him) that he said: "An hour's reflection is better than a year's worship."

Ibn al-Qasim related from Malik, who said: It was said to Umm al-Darda': What was the most frequent of Abu al-Darda's concerns? She said: The most frequent of his concerns was reflection. It was said to him: Do you consider reflection to be one of the deeds? He said: Yes, it is certainty (al-yaqin).

Ibn al-Musayyab was asked about prayer between Dhuhr and Asr. He said: This is not worship. Worship is abstaining from what Allah has forbidden and reflecting on the command of Allah.

Al-Hasan said: An hour's reflection is better than a night of standing in prayer. Ibn Abbas and Abu al-Darda' said the same. Al-Hasan also said: Reflection is the mirror of the believer, in which he looks at his good deeds and his bad deeds.

Among the things one reflects upon are the fears of the Hereafter: the gathering and the resurrection, Paradise and its bliss, and the Fire and its punishment.

It is reported that Abu Sulayman al-Darani (may Allah be pleased with him) took a vessel of water to perform ablution for the night prayer, and a guest was with him. The guest saw that when he inserted his finger into the handle of the vessel, he remained in reflection about that until dawn broke. He said to him: What is this, O Abu Sulayman? He said: When I put my finger into the handle of the vessel, I reflected on the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿When the shackles are around their necks and the chains, they will be dragged.﴾ [al-Mu'min: 71] [[See vol. 15, p. 332.]] I reflected on my own state and how I would bear the iron collar if it were placed around my neck on the Day of Resurrection. I continued in that until morning came.

Ibn Atiyya said: "This is the extreme of fear, but the best of matters is their middle course. The scholars of the community, who are the proof, do not follow this method. The study of the knowledge of the Book of Allah and the meanings of the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is, for one who understands and whose benefit is hoped for, better than this."

Ibn al-Arabi said: People have disagreed about which of the two acts is better: reflection or prayer. The Sufis held that reflection is better, for it yields knowledge (ma'rifa), which is the most excellent of the legal stations (al-maqamat al-shar'iyya). The jurists (fuqaha') held that prayer is better, because of what has come in the hadith urging it, calling to it, and encouraging it. In the two Sahihs, from Ibn Abbas, it is related that he spent the night at the house of his aunt Maymuna. In it is: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) got up, wiped sleep from his face, recited the last ten verses of Surat Al 'Imran, went to a hanging water skin [[al-shann: the water skin.]], performed a light ablution, and then prayed thirteen rak'ahs, and so on in the hadith. So consider, may Allah have mercy on you, how he combined reflection on the created things with then turning to his prayer afterward. This is the Sunnah on which reliance is placed.

As for the way of the Sufis, in which a shaykh spends a day, a night, or a month continuously reflecting without slackening, this is a path far from correctness, unsuitable for human beings, and not consistent with the Sunnah.

Ibn Atiyya said: My father related to me from some scholars of the East, who said: I was spending the night in the Masjid al-Aqdam [[Masjid al-Aqdam: a mosque in the vicinity of Old Cairo, near the fountain of Ibn Tulun. See al-Maqrizi, vol. 2, p. 445, Bulaq edition.]] in Egypt. I prayed the ʿishā' prayer, and I saw a man who had lain down in a cloak, covering himself with it, until morning. We prayed that night. When the dawn prayer was called, that man rose, faced the qibla, and prayed with the people. I was amazed at his boldness in praying without ablution. When the prayer ended, he went out, and I followed him to admonish him. When I drew near to him, I heard him reciting poetry:

His body is covered, yet he is absent and present,
his heart is awake, silent, and mindful.
Contracted in the unseen, yet expanded;
so is the one who knows and remembers.
He spends his night as one devoted to reflection,
so he is, all night, a sleeper, yet skilled.

He said: I knew that he was one of those who worship through reflection, so I withdrew from him.

The ninth issue: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, You did not create this in vain﴾, meaning they say: You did not create it as a pointless or frivolous thing, but You created it as a sign of Your power and wisdom. Al-batil is that which is transient and passes away. From this is the saying of Labid:

Surely everything other than Allah is vain (batil), meaning transient.

"Batilan" is in the accusative because it is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun (maṣdar), meaning "a vain creation." It has also been said that it is in the accusative by the removal of the preposition, meaning: You did not create it for vanity. It has also been said that it is the second object, with "khalaqa" meaning "ja'ala" (made).

(Subḥānaka) Al-Nahhas related through Musa ibn Talha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the meaning of "Subhan Allah," and he said: "The glorification of Allah above evil." Its meaning has already been fully explained in al-Baqara [[See vol. 1, p. 276.]]. (Fa-qina 'adhab al-nar) means: save us from its punishment. This has already been mentioned [[See vol. 2, p. 433.]].

The tenth issue: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, whoever You admit to the Fire, You have indeed disgraced him﴾. Akhzaytahu means: You humiliated him and degraded him. Al-Mufaddal said: It means You destroyed him, and he recited:

May God disgrace from the cross His servants,
and those who wear the caps of the monks.

It has also been said: You exposed him and removed him far away. One says: "Akhzahu Allah" means Allah removed him far away and abhorred him. The noun is "al-khizy." Ibn al-Sikkit said: "Khaziya yakhza khizyan" means he fell into a calamity. Those who hold to the doctrine of threat (ashab al-wa'id) have relied on this verse and said: Whoever is admitted to the Fire should not be a believer, because of His saying: "You have disgraced him." But Allah says: ﴿On the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him﴾ [al-Tahrim: 8] [[See vol. 18, p. 791.]]. What they said is rejected, because the evidences establish that whoever commits a grave sin does not lose the name of faith, as has already been mentioned and will come.

What is meant by His saying "whoever You admit to the Fire" is "whoever You make abide eternally in the Fire." This was said by Anas ibn Malik. Qatada said: "Tudkhil" is the inverted form of "tukhalladu" (You make abide), and we do not say as the people of Harura said. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: The verse is specific to a people who will not come out of the Fire, and for this reason He said: ﴿And the wrongdoers have no helpers﴾, meaning the disbelievers.

The people of the meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: "Khizy" may mean shame. One says: "Khaziya yakhza khizayatan" when he was ashamed, so he is "khazyan." Dhu al-Rumma said:

A shame overtook him at his fall,
from the side of the rope, mixed with it was anger.

So the disgrace of the believers on that Day will be their shame at entering the Fire among the rest of the people of the religions, until they come out of it. The disgrace of the disbelievers is their destruction therein without death, whereas the believers die, and thus they differ. This is established in the authentic Sunnah from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, which Muslim recorded, and it has already been mentioned and will come.

The eleventh issue: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, we have indeed heard a caller calling to faith﴾. The caller means Muhammad (ﷺ), as said by Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, and most of the exegetes. Qatada and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: It is the Qur'an, and not all of them heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The evidence for this view is what Allah the Exalted related about the believing jinn when they said: ﴿Indeed we heard a wondrous Qur'an, guiding to right conduct﴾ [al-Jinn: 1-2] [[See vol. 19, p. 6.]]. The earlier scholars answered: Whoever hears the Qur'an is as if he met the Prophet (ﷺ), and this is correct in meaning. "Li-l-iman" (to faith) is, from "an amminu" (that believe), in a place of accusative by the omission of the preposition, meaning "bi-an amanu" (that they believe). In the speech there is an inversion, meaning: we heard a caller calling to faith, calling, according to Abu Ubayda. It has also been said: the lam has the meaning of "ila" (to), meaning "to faith," like His saying: ﴿Then they return to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-Mujadila: 8] [[See vol. 17, p. 290.]], and His saying: ﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾ [al-Zalzala: 5] [[See vol. 20, p. 140.]], and His saying: ﴿Praise be to Allah who guided us to this﴾ [al-A'raf: 43] [[See vol. 7, p. 802.]], meaning "to this," and the like of it is abundant. It has also been said: it is the lam of purpose (lam al-ajl), meaning "for the sake of faith."

The twelfth issue: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, so forgive us our sins and remove from us our misdeeds﴾. This is emphasis and intensification in supplication. The meanings of the two expressions are one, for "al-ghafr" and "al-kafr" both mean covering.

(And cause us to die with the righteous) meaning: as righteous ones along with the prophets, that is, among their company. Its singular is "barr" and "barr" (pious), and its root is from expansiveness, as if the pious one is expansive in obedience to Allah and Allah's mercy is expansive toward him.

The thirteenth issue: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾, meaning: upon the tongues of Your messengers, like "wa-sal al-qarya" [[See vol. 9, p. 245.]]. Al-A'mash and al-Zuhri read "rusulika" (rusl-ika) with the lightened form, and this refers to what has been mentioned of the seeking of forgiveness by the prophets and the angels for the believers, for the angels seek forgiveness for those on earth. It also refers to what has been mentioned of Nuh's supplication for the believers, Ibrahim's supplication, and the Prophet's (ﷺ) seeking forgiveness for his community.

(And do not disgrace us), meaning: do not punish us, do not destroy us, do not expose us, do not humiliate us, do not remove us far away, and do not make us abhorred on the Day of Resurrection. (Indeed You do not fail in the promise.) If it is asked: What is the meaning of their saying ﴿Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 194], when they know that He does not fail in the promise? The answer has three aspects. The first: Allah, glorified is He, promised Paradise to whoever believes, so they asked to be among those who were promised that, rather than disgrace and punishment.

The second: They made this supplication as an act of worship and humility, and supplication is the marrow of worship. This is like His saying: ﴿He said: My Lord, judge with truth﴾ [al-Anbiya': 112] [[According to the reading of Nafi'. See vol. 11, p. 351.]], although He judges only with truth.

The third: They asked to be given what they had been promised of victory over their enemy promptly, because this is a report about the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), and they asked this for the sake of exalting the religion. And Allah knows best.

Anas ibn Malik related that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, promises a reward for a deed, He will certainly fulfill it out of mercy; and whoever He promises a punishment for a deed, then He has the choice in it." The Arabs censure breaking a promise, and they praise doing so in a threat, until one of them said [[He is ʿAmir ibn al-Tufayl, as in Lisan al-ʿArab.]]:

The cousin does not fear, as long as I live, my assault,
nor do I hide from the fear of the one who threatens.
And if ever I threaten him or promise him,
I am one who breaks my threat and fulfills my promise.

[Thirteenth to twenty-third points, continued]

The fourteenth point concerns His words, may He be exalted: ﴿So their Lord answered them﴾, meaning He responded to them. Al-Hasan said: "They continued saying 'Our Lord, our Lord' until He answered them." Ja'far al-Sadiq said: "Whoever is afflicted by a matter [[hazaba al-amr: when a serious matter befalls him or distress strikes him]] and says five times, 'Our Lord,' Allah will deliver him from what he fears and grant him what he wants." It was asked: "How is that?" He said: "Recite, if you wish: ﴿Those who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides — to His words: Indeed You do not fail in the promise﴾ [Al 'Imran: 191–194]."

The fifteenth point concerns His words: ﴿that I﴾, meaning "that I." 'Isa ibn 'Umar read "Inni" with a kasra on the hamza, meaning "so He said: Indeed I." Al-Hakim Abu 'Abd Allah related in his Sahih from Umm Salamah that she said: "O Messenger of Allah, do I not hear that Allah mentions women in emigration in any way?" Then Allah, may He be exalted, revealed: ﴿So their Lord answered them, that I do not waste the work of any worker among you, whether male or female﴾ [the verse]. It was also related by al-Tirmidhi. The particle "min" entered for emphasis, because before it there is a negative particle. The Kufans said: it is for explanation and it is not permissible to omit it, because it entered for a meaning without which the speech would not be sound; it is only omitted when it is for emphasis of negation.

﴿Some of you are from some﴾ is a subject and predicate, meaning your religion is one. It was also said: some of you are from some in reward, rulings, support and the like. Al-Dahhak said: "Your men are like your women in obedience, and your women are like your men in obedience." A parallel to this is His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another﴾ [al-Tawbah: 71] [[See vol. 8, p. 202.]]. It is also said: "So-and-so is from me," meaning he is upon my way and my character.

The sixteenth point concerns His words: ﴿So those who emigrated﴾, a subject and predicate, meaning they left their homelands and traveled to Madinah.

﴿And were driven out of their homes﴾ in obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And fought﴾, meaning and fought My enemies.

﴿And were killed﴾, meaning in My cause. Ibn Kathir and Ibn 'Amir read "wa qatalu wa quttilu" with intensification. Al-A'mash read "wa qutilu wa qatalu," because the conjunction "wa" does not indicate that the second occurred after the first. It was also said: there is an implied "qad" in the speech, meaning "were killed, when they had fought," and from this is the poet's saying:

He acted youthful, while old age had overtaken him,

meaning "and old age had already overtaken him." It was also said: meaning that those among them who remained fought, as the Arabs say, "We killed the Banu Tamim," though only some of them were killed. Imru' al-Qays said:

If you fight us, we will kill you.

'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz read "wa qatalu wa qutilu" with light pronunciation and without an alif.

﴿I will surely remove from them their misdeeds﴾, meaning I will veil them for them in the Hereafter, so I will neither rebuke them for them nor punish them for them.

﴿As a reward from Allah﴾: it is an emphatic infinitive according to the Basrans, because the meaning of "I will surely admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow" is "I will surely reward them with a reward." Al-Kisa'i said: it is in the accusative as a qat' (a clarifying detached element). Al-Farra' said: it is in the accusative as tafsir (explanation).

﴿And with Allah is the best reward﴾, meaning the best recompense, which is what returns to the doer from the fruit of his deed, from thaba yathubu (to return).

The seventeenth point concerns His words: ﴿Let not the movement of those who disbelieve throughout the land deceive you﴾. It was said: the address is to the Prophet ﷺ and the intended meaning is the community. It was also said: it is addressed to everyone. This is because the Muslims said: "These disbelievers have caravans, wealth and movement in the lands, while we have perished from hunger." So this verse was revealed, meaning: let not their safety through their travels deceive you.

﴿A little enjoyment﴾, meaning their movement is a little enjoyment. Ya'qub read "yaghurrannaka" with a sukun on the nun, and he recited:

Let not the evening of a resident deceive you, for dawn may meet you with death.

A parallel to this verse is His words: ﴿So let not their movement in the lands deceive you﴾ [Ghafir: 4] [[See vol. 15, p. 286.]]. Al-matA' (enjoyment) is that whose benefit is quickly obtained, and He called it little because it is perishable, and every perishable thing, even if abundant, is little. In the Sahih of al-Tirmidhi, from al-Mustawrid al-Fihri, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "The world compared with the Hereafter is nothing but what one of you would obtain by dipping his finger in the sea; let him look at what it returns with." It was said: "yarji'u" is read with ya and with ta.

﴿And evil is the resting place﴾, meaning evil is what they prepared for themselves by their disbelief, and what Allah has prepared for them of the Fire.

The eighteenth point: in this verse and similar ones, such as His words: ﴿Indeed, what We give them respite for is better for them﴾ [Al 'Imran: 178] [[See p. 286 of this part.]], and ﴿I give them respite, indeed My plan is firm﴾ [al-A'raf: 183] [[See vol. 7, pp. 329 and 237.]], and ﴿Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 55] [[See vol. 12, p. 130.]], and ﴿We will lead them step by step from where they do not know﴾ [al-A'raf: 182] [[See vol. 7, pp. 329 and 237.]], there is evidence that the disbelievers are not favored in this world. This is because the true essence of a blessing is being free of the harms that are immediate and deferred, whereas the blessings of the disbelievers are mixed with pains and punishments. So it is like one who sets before another a sweet of honey in which there is poison: though its eater enjoys it, one does not say "he has bestowed a favor upon him," because in it is the destruction of his soul. This is the view of a group of scholars, and it is the statement of Shaykh Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari. But a group among them, the Sword of the Sunnah and Tongue of the Community, Qadi Abu Bakr, held that Allah did bestow favors upon them in this world. They said: the root of "ni'mah" (blessing) is from "na'mah" with a fatha on the nun, which is ease of living, and from this is His words: ﴿And luxury they were in, enjoying fruits﴾ [al-Dukhan: 27] [[See vol. 16, p. 138.]]. One says "daqiq na'im" when the flour is ground thoroughly and finely sifted. This is the correct view, and the evidence for it is that Allah obliged the disbelievers to thank Him, as He obliged all the responsible: ﴿So remember the favors of Allah﴾ [al-A'raf: 74] [[See vol. 7, pp. 329 and 237.]], ﴿And be grateful to Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 172] [[See vol. 2, p. 215.]]. Thanks is only for a blessing. He also said: ﴿And do good as Allah has done good to you﴾ [al-Qasas: 77] [[See vol. 13, p. 314.]], and this is addressed to Qarun. He said: ﴿And Allah presents an example: a town that was secure and tranquil﴾ [al-Nahl: 112] [[See vol. 10, pp. 193 and 166.]], the verse. Thus He alerted that He had bestowed on them a worldly blessing, which they denied. He said: ﴿They recognize the blessing of Allah, then deny it﴾ [al-Nahl: 83] [[See vol. 10, pp. 193 and 166.]]. He said: ﴿O people, remember the blessing of Allah upon you﴾ [Fatir: 3] [[See vol. 14, p. 321.]]. This is general for disbelievers and others. As for one who offers another food containing poison, he has treated him gently in the moment, since he did not make him swallow pure poison but concealed it in sweetness; so it is not far-fetched to say, "he has bestowed a favor upon him." If this is established, then blessings are of two kinds: blessings of benefit and blessings of repelling. The blessings of benefit are what reaches them of kinds of pleasures, and the blessings of repelling are what is turned away from them of kinds of calamities. On this basis Allah has bestowed upon the disbelievers blessings of repelling, by unanimous agreement, namely what is averted from them of pains and illnesses, and there is no disagreement among them that He did not bestow upon them the blessing of His religion. And praise is to Allah.

The nineteenth point concerns His words: ﴿But those who fear their Lord﴾. It is an exception (istidrak) after a statement that carried the sense of negation, because the meaning of what came before is that they have no great benefit from their movement in the lands, but for the God-fearing there is great benefit and eternal abiding. So the position of "lakin" is nominative by inception. Yazid ibn al-Qa'qa' read "lakinna" with the nun doubled.

The twentieth point concerns His words: ﴿A welcome gift from Allah﴾. Nuzulan is like thawaban according to the Basrans; according to al-Kisa'i it is a verbal noun. Al-Farra' said: it is an explanatory element. Al-Hasan and al-Nakha'i read "nuzulan" with the zay lightened, finding two dammas burdensome; the rest read it with the zay heavy. The nuzul is what is prepared for the guest, and the nazil is the guest. The poet said:

The guest of a people is the greatest of them in rights, and the right of Allah is in the right of the guest.

The plural is al-anzal. "Hazzun nazil" means gathered. Nuzul (with dhamma then sukun, or with fatha) also means the surplus, and one says "food of nuzul and nuzl."

The twenty-first point: I say, perhaps the nuzul, and Allah knows best, is what came in the Sahih of Muslim from the hadith of Thawban, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in the story of the rabbi who asked the Prophet ﷺ: "Where will people be on the day the earth is changed to other than the earth and the heavens?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "They will be in darkness beyond the bridge." He said: "Who among the people will cross first?" He said: "The poor among the emigrants." The Jew said: "What is their gift (tuhfah) when they enter Paradise?" He said: "The extra piece of the liver of the fish (ziyadat kabid al-nun)." He said: "What is their food after it?" He said: "The bull of Paradise will be slaughtered for them, which used to graze on its outskirts." He said: "What is their drink with it?" He said: "From a spring in it called Salsabil," and he mentioned the hadith. The lexicographers said: the tuhfah is what a person is presented with of fruits, and the tarf is its finest and most delicate things, and this matches what we mentioned concerning the nuzul. And Allah knows best. Ziyadat al-kabid is a piece of it like a finger. Al-Harawi said: "A welcome gift from Allah," meaning a reward; it was also said, provision.

﴿And what is with Allah is better for the righteous﴾, meaning better than what the disbelievers enjoy in this world. And Allah knows best.

The twenty-second point concerns His words: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Book are those who believe in Allah﴾, the verse. Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, Anas, Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah and al-Hasan said: it was revealed concerning the Negus, because when he died Jibril, peace be upon him, informed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of his death, and the Prophet ﷺ said to his companions: "Stand and pray over your brother the Negus." Some of them said to others: "He orders us to pray over a non-Arab, one of the uncouth Abyssinians." So Allah revealed: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Book are those who believe in Allah and in what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them.﴾ Al-Dahhak said: "what has been revealed to you" is the Qur'an.

﴿And what has been revealed to them﴾ is the Torah and the Gospel. In the Revelation: ﴿Those will be given their reward twice﴾ [al-Qasas: 54] [[See vol. 13, p. 297.]]. In the Sahih of Muslim: "Three will be given their reward twice," and he mentioned them, including "a man of the People of the Book who believed in his prophet, then encountered the Prophet ﷺ, believed in him, followed him and affirmed him; he has two rewards," and he related the hadith. Prayer over him and what scholars hold regarding prayer over an absent deceased have already been discussed in al-Baqarah, so there is no point in repeating it. Mujahid, Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd said: it was revealed concerning believers among the People of the Book, and this is general, and the Negus is one of them. His name was Ashamah, which in Arabic is 'Ata'ah (gift). And ﴿humble﴾ means lowly, and it is accusative as a circumstantial state (hal) of the pronoun in "yu'minu." It was also said: it is a state of the pronoun in "ilayhim" or "ilaykum." What is in the verse is clear, and it has already been discussed.

The twenty-third point concerns His words: ﴿O you who believe, persevere﴾, the verse. Allah concluded the sura with what this tenth verse includes of the admonitions that gather victory in this world over enemies and success with the bliss of the Hereafter. He urged patience in obedience and restraint from desires. Patience is restraint, and its explanation has already been given in al-Baqarah [[See vol. 2, p. 174.]]. He commanded mutual steadfastness (musabarah), and it was said its meaning is steadfastness against enemies; this was said by Zayd ibn Aslam.

Al-Hasan said: "[It means] the five daily prayers." It was also said: "[It means] persistent opposition to the self in its desires, for it calls to them while he restrains it."

ʿAtaʾ and al-Qurazi said: "Be patient in the face of the promise that was made to you," i.e., do not despair, and await relief. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Waiting for relief with patience is an act of worship." Abu ʿUmar (Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr), may Allah have mercy on him, preferred this view. The first view is the view of the majority, and from it is the verse of ʿAntarah:

"I have not seen living people who endure as we endure,
nor who confront as those we confront."

His words "endure as we endure" mean: they endured the enemy in war, and no cowardice or weakness appeared from them. "Mukafahah" means facing and confronting one another in battle. For this reason they differed concerning the meaning of His words (wa-rabitu) ["and be steadfast in readiness"]. The majority of the community said: "Be steadfast in readiness against your enemies with horses," i.e., tie up horses as your enemies tie them up. From it is the words of the Most High: ﴿And of steeds held in readiness﴾ [al-Anfal: 60] [[See vol. 8, p. 36.]]

In the Muwatta' of Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: Abu ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrah wrote to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab mentioning the armies of the Romans and what he feared from them. ʿUmar wrote to him: "To proceed: whatever hardship befalls a believing servant, Allah will make relief after it, and indeed one hardship will never overcome two eases. Allah the Most High says in His Book: ﴿O you who believe, be patient, endure in patience, be steadfast in readiness, and fear Allah that you may be successful﴾."

Abu Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman said: this verse concerns waiting for prayer after prayer, and there was no campaign in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in which one stayed in readiness. Al-Hakim Abu ʿAbd Allah related it in his Sahih. Abu Salamah cited his (peace be upon him) saying: "Shall I not direct you to that by which Allah erases sins and raises ranks? Performing ablution thoroughly despite hardship, walking many steps to the mosques, and waiting for prayer after prayer—that is steadfastness in readiness" (repeated three times). Related by Malik.

Ibn ʿAtiyyah said: The correct view is that ribat [here, "ribat" is from the manuscripts B, J, H, and T] is constant attachment in the way of Allah. Its origin is from tying horses, then every one constantly stationed at a frontier of the frontiers of Islam [in B: "the Muslims"] was called murabit, whether mounted or on foot. The term is derived from rabt (tying). The saying of the Prophet ﷺ "that is ribat" is only a figurative comparison to ribat in the way of Allah. The lexical ribat is the first meaning, and this is [in B: "thus"] like his saying: "The strong man is not the one who overthrows others" [sur'ah, one who is never defeated in wrestling], and his saying: "The poor man is not this wanderer," and so on.

I say: His words "The lexical ribat is the first meaning" are not accepted, for al-Khalil ibn Ahmad, one of the imams and trustworthy authorities of the language, said: ribat is constant presence at the frontiers, and also persistence in prayer. Thus waiting for prayer is literally ribat, as the Prophet ﷺ said. More than this is what al-Shaybani said: it is said "maʾ mutarabit," i.e., water that is perpetual and never drawn off. Ibn Faris related it, and this requires extending the lexical meaning of ribat beyond what we have mentioned. For among the Arabs, murabatah is binding a thing firmly so that it does not come loose and return to what one has been patient about, thus holding the heart to good intention and the body to obedience. Among its greatest and most important forms is tying horses in the way of Allah, as explicitly stated in revelation in His words: ﴿And of steeds held in readiness﴾ [al-Anfal: 60], as will come. Binding the self to the prayers is as the Prophet ﷺ said, related by Abu Hurayrah, Jabir and ʿAli, and "there is no perfume after a bride."

Twenty-fourth issue: The one stationed in the way of Allah, according to the jurists, is the one who travels to a frontier to remain there for a period of time, as said by Muhammad ibn al-Mawwaz [and he related it]. As for the permanent residents of the frontiers with their families, who build and earn their living there, although they are protectors they are not stationed (murabitun). Ibn ʿAtiyyah said: Ibn Khuwayz Mindad said: ribat has two states: a state in which the frontier is secure and impregnable, where it is permissible to settle there with family and children; and if it is not secure, it is permissible for one who is fit for fighting to station himself there personally, but he should not bring family and children there, lest the enemy prevail, take captives and enslave them. And Allah knows best.

Twenty-fifth issue: Many hadiths have come concerning the merit of ribat, among them what al-Bukhari related from Sahl ibn Saʿd al-Saʿidi that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A day of ribat in the way of Allah is better with Allah than the world and all that is in it." And in Sahih Muslim, from Salman, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "A day and a night of ribat is better than a month of fasting and standing in prayer by night for it, and if he dies, his deeds which he used to do continue for him, his provision is continued for him, and he is safe from the tempter." [[al-Fattan: the Devil. It is related with a fatha and with a damma on the fa. Whoever reads it with fatha means a single one, because he tempts people away from religion. Whoever reads it with damma means the plural of fatin, i.e., they assist one another in misleading people from the truth and tempting them.]] Abu Dawud related in his Sunan from Fadalah ibn ʿUbayd that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Every dead person has his deeds sealed except the one stationed (murabit), for his deed continues to grow for him until the Day of Resurrection, and he is safe from the tormentor of the grave."

In these two hadiths there is evidence that ribat is the best of the deeds whose reward remains after death, as came in the hadith of al-ʿAla' ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "When a person dies, his deeds are cut off except from three: ongoing charity, knowledge from which benefit is gained, or a righteous child who prays for him." [[This is the narration of Muslim as in the Kitab al-Wasiyyah. Likewise in Z, T, Ha, J. In another narration: "Ibn Adam." The hadith was related by al-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i with the wording: "except from three: charity..." and al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad.]] It is a sound hadith, related by Muslim alone. The ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge and righteous child who prays for his parents are cut off by the exhaustion of charities, the passing of knowledge and the death of the child. But the reward of ribat is multiplied until the Day of Resurrection, for growth has no meaning except multiplication, and this is not conditional upon a cause that would be cut off when it ends; rather it is a perpetual bounty from Allah the Most High until the Day of Resurrection. This is because all acts of righteousness can only be undertaken with safety from the enemy and guarding against it, by protecting the core of religion and upholding the symbols of Islam. The deed whose reward continues is what he used to do of righteous deeds. Ibn Majah related with a sound chain from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Whoever dies while stationed in the way of Allah, the reward of the righteous deed he used to do continues for him, his provision continues for him, he is safe from the tempter, and Allah will raise him on the Day of Resurrection secure from terror." In this hadith there is a second condition, which is death in the state of ribat. And Allah knows best.

It is related from ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Whoever stations himself for one night in the way of Allah, it is for him like a thousand nights of fasting and standing in prayer."

It is related from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, a day of ribat in the way of Allah, guarding the weak point of the Muslims, seeking reward, other than in Ramadan, is greater in reward than a hundred years of worship, fasting and standing in prayer. And a day of ribat in the way of Allah, guarding the weak point of the Muslims, seeking reward, in Ramadan, is better with Allah and greater in reward—I think he said: than a thousand years of worship, fasting and standing in prayer. If Allah returns him safe to his family, no sin is recorded against him for a thousand years, and good deeds are recorded for him, and the reward of ribat continues for him until the Day of Resurrection." [[The narration of Ibn Majah.]]

This hadith indicates that a day of ribat in Ramadan obtains lasting reward even if one does not die while stationed.

And Allah knows best. It is related from Anas ibn Malik who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Guarding one night in the way of Allah is better than a man's fasting and standing in prayer with his family for a thousand years; the year is three hundred and sixty days, and the day is like a thousand years." [[In J.]]

I say: It has also come concerning waiting for prayer after prayer that it is ribat, so the one who awaits the prayers may attain that merit, if Allah the Most High wills. Abu Nuʿaym al-Hafiz related: Sulayman ibn Ahmad told us, ʿAli ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz told us, Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal told us [ḥ — the transition mark used by hadith scholars when a hadith has two or more chains, read as "al-hadith" by the reciter, as explained in the note]; and Abu Bakr ibn Malik told us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal told us, my father told me, al-Hasan ibn Musa told me, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Abu Ayyub al-Azdi, from Nawf al-Bikali, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, that the Prophet ﷺ prayed Maghrib one night and we prayed with him. Some people remained for supererogatory prayer and some went home. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came before the people had turned to the ʿIsha' prayer, and came while the people were present, raising his finger, having counted twenty-nine, pointing with the index finger to the sky. He drew up his garment from his knees and said: "Rejoice, assembly of Muslims! This is your Lord who has opened a gate of the gates of heaven, boasting of you to the angels, saying: O My angels, look at these servants of Mine, who have completed an obligatory prayer while awaiting another."

Hammad ibn Salamah related it from ʿAli ibn Zayd from Mutarrif ibn ʿAbd Allah: that Nawf and ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr met, and Nawf related from the Torah, and ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr related this hadith from the Prophet ﷺ.

(And fear Allah) i.e., you were not commanded to fight without taqwa.

(That you may be successful) so that you may be hopeful of success. It was also said: la'alla means li-kay (in order that). Al-falah is endurance (baqa'). All of this has passed in al-Baqarah in full detail [[See vol. 1, pp. 162, 182, 227.]], and praise be to Allah.

The commentary on Surah Al ʿImran has been completed from (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran wa-l-Mubayyin lima Tadammana min al-Sunnah wa-Ayi al-Furqan), by the grace and help of Allah.

Verified by Abu Ishaq Ibrahim al-Tafayyash.

The fourth part of the Tafsir of al-Qurtubi is complete, followed, God willing, by the fifth part. Surah al-Nisa' — by Allah's help and gracious guidance. The fourth part of the book (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) of al-Qurtubi, fifth part, has been printed.

**Question 1:** There are twenty-five issues in this passage. The first is the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾. The meaning of this verse has already been discussed in *al-Baqarah* (see vol. 2, p. 191) and in other places. Allah concluded this surah by commanding contemplation and reasoning about His signs, since these signs can only proceed from a Living, Self-Subsisting, All-Powerful, Holy, Peaceful One who is free of need from the worlds, so that their faith may rest on certainty and not on mere imitation (taqlid).

﴿Are signs for those of understanding﴾: those who use their minds to reflect on the proofs. It is narrated from ʿAishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: When this verse was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ, he stood to pray. Bilal came to inform him of the prayer and saw him weeping. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, do you weep when Allah has forgiven you your earlier and later sins?" He said: "O Bilal, should I not be a grateful servant? Allah has revealed to me tonight a verse: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, are signs for those of understanding﴾." Then he said: "Woe to the one who recites it and does not reflect upon it."

**Question 2:** The scholars said: It is recommended for one who wakes from sleep to wipe his face and to begin his night prayer by reciting these ten verses, following the example of the Prophet ﷺ. This is established in the *Sahihayn* (al-Bukhari and Muslim) and elsewhere, and it will come. Then he prays what has been decreed for him. Thus he combines reflection and action, and this is the best of deeds [17 line deleted in the manuscript] whose explanation will come in this verse after this.

It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite ten verses from the end of *Al ʿImran* every night. Abu Nasr al-Wa'ili al-Sijistani, the hafiz, recorded it in his book *al-Ibanah* from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Musa, from Muzahir ibn Aslam al-Makhzumi, from al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurairah. The beginning of the surah has already been discussed (see p. 2 of this part) regarding ʿUthman, who said: Whoever recites the end of *Al ʿImran* in a night, the reward of a night of prayer is written for him.

**Question 3:** The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Those who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides﴾. Allah mentioned three states in which the son of Adam does not usually fail to be, in most of his affairs, so these states seem to encompass his time. In this sense is the saying of ʿAishah, may Allah be pleased with her: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to remember Allah in all his states." It was recorded by Muslim. This includes his being in the toilet and other situations.

The scholars differed on this. ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr, Ibn Sirin, and al-Nakhaʿi permitted it, while Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAta', and al-Shaʿbi disliked it. The first view is more correct because of the generality of the verse and the hadith. Al-Nakhaʿi said: "There is no harm in remembering Allah in the toilet, for it rises," meaning: it rises (to Allah) with the angels, written in their scrolls, so the word "it" is an omitted noun (the remembrance). The evidence is the words of Allah: ﴿Not a word does he utter but that with him is an observer, ready﴾ [Qaf: 18], and His words: ﴿And indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording﴾ [al-Infitar: 10–11]. Also, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded His servants to remember Him in every state without exception, saying: ﴿Remember Allah with much remembrance﴾ [al-Ahzab: 41], and: ﴿So remember Me; I will remember you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 152], and: ﴿Indeed, We do not allow the reward of those who do good to be lost﴾ [al-Kahf: 30]. Thus the command is general. So the one who remembers Allah in all his states is rewarded, if Allah wills.

Abu Nuʿaym reported: Abu Bakr ibn Malik narrated to us, ʿAbdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from ʿAta' ibn Abi Marwan, from his father, from Kaʿb al-Ahbar, who said: Musa, peace be upon him, said: "O Lord, are You near so that I may whisper to You, or far so that I may call out to You?" He said: "O Musa, I am the companion of the one who remembers Me." He said: "O Lord, we are in states in which we would honor You and glorify You by not remembering You." He said: "What are they?" He said: "Sexual impurity and defecation." He said: "O Musa, remember Me in every state."

The dislike of those who disliked it is either out of glorifying the remembrance of Allah in places where it is disliked to mention Him, like the dislike of reciting the Qur'an in the bathhouse, or out of sparing the noble recording angels from being placed in places of filth and impurity while writing what is uttered. And Allah knows best.

The phrase "standing and sitting" is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl).

﴿And on their sides﴾: in the position of a circumstantial clause, meaning: and lying down. A similar expression is the words of Allah: ﴿He calls Us, whether lying on his side or sitting or standing﴾ [Yunus: 12], in reverse order, meaning: He called Us while lying on his side.

A group of commentators, including al-Hasan and others, held that the words "they remember Allah" to the end refer to the prayer, meaning: they do not neglect it. In a state of excuse, they pray sitting or on their sides. This is like the words of Allah: ﴿So when you have finished the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides﴾ [al-Nisa': 103], according to the view of Ibn Masʿud, as will be explained. If the verse concerns prayer, its jurisprudence is that a person prays standing; if he cannot, then sitting; if he cannot, then on his side. This is as established from ʿImran ibn Husayn, who said: I had hemorrhoids, so I asked the Prophet ﷺ about prayer, and he said: "Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; if you cannot, then on your side." The imams related it. The Prophet ﷺ used to pray sitting in optional prayers a year before his death, as is in *Sahih Muslim*. Al-Nasa'i narrated from ʿAishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ praying cross-legged." Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman (al-Nasa'i's kunyah) said: "I know of no one who narrated this hadith except Abu Dawud al-Hafari (a nisbah to a place in Kufa; his name is ʿUmar ibn Saʿd ibn ʿUbayd), and he is trustworthy, but I do not think this hadith is anything but an error. And Allah knows best."

**Question 4:** The scholars differed on the manner and form of the prayer of the sick and of the one who sits. Ibn ʿAbd al-Hakam reported from Malik that he sits cross-legged while standing. Al-Buwayti reported from al-Shafiʿi: "When he wants to prostrate, he prepares himself for prostration according to what he can bear." He said: "The same applies to one praying an optional prayer." Similar is the view of al-Thawri. Likewise said al-Layth, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad. Al-Shafiʿi in the narration of al-Muzani said: He sits throughout his entire prayer as one sits for the tashahhud. This was also reported from Malik and his companions, but the first, which is well-known (in the school, al-madhhab; this was corrected in the margin), is the apparent view of the *Mudawwanah*. Abu Hanifah and Zufar said: He sits as one sits for the tashahhud, and similarly he bows and prostrates (while sitting).

**Question 5:** He said: If he cannot sit, he prays on his side or his back, by choice. This is the position of the *Mudawwanah*. Ibn Habib related from Ibn al-Qasim: He prays on his back; if he cannot, then on his right side; then on his left side. In the book of Ibn al-Mawwaz it is the reverse: he prays on his right side, otherwise on his left, otherwise on his back. Sahnun said: He prays on his right side, as he is placed in his grave, otherwise on his back, otherwise on his left. Malik and Abu Hanifah said: When one prays lying down, his feet should be toward the qiblah. Al-Shafiʿi and al-Thawri said: He prays on his side with his face toward the qiblah.

**Question 6:** If he regains strength during the prayer because the illness has lessened, Ibn al-Qasim said: He stands for the rest of his prayer and builds on what has passed. This is also the view of al-Shafiʿi, Zufar, and al-Tabari. Abu Hanifah and his two companions, Yaʿqub and Muhammad, said regarding one who prayed one rak'ah lying down and then recovered: he must begin the prayer again from its beginning. But if he was praying sitting, bowing and prostrating, and then recovered, he builds upon it according to Abu Hanifah, and does not build upon it according to Muhammad. Abu Hanifah and his companions said: If one begins the prayer standing and then reaches the point of gesturing (iʾma'), he should continue building on it. This was narrated from Abu Yusuf. Malik said regarding the sick person who cannot bow or prostrate, but can stand and sit: he prays standing and gestures for bowing; when he wants to prostrate, he sits and gestures for prostration. This is also the view of Abu Yusuf and the analogy of al-Shafiʿi's view. Abu Hanifah and his companions said: He prays sitting.

**Question 7:** As for the prayer of the one who sleeps while healthy: there is an addition narrated in the hadith of ʿImran ibn Husayn that is not found elsewhere: "The prayer of the one who sleeps is like half the prayer of the one who sits." Abu ʿUmar said: The majority of scholars do not permit optional prayer while lying down. This hadith was not narrated except by Husayn al-Muʿallim, namely Husayn ibn Dhakwan, from ʿAbdullah ibn Buraydah, from ʿImran ibn Husayn. It has been disputed regarding its chain and its text in a way that requires caution about it. If it is authentic, I do not know its meaning. If any of the scholars permitted optional prayer lying down for one who is able to sit or stand, then its basis is this addition in the report, and it is the evidence for those who hold that view. But if they agreed on the dislike of optional prayer while lying down for one able to sit or stand, then the hadith of Husayn is either an error or abrogated.

It was also said: The meaning of the verse is those who infer from the creation of the heavens and the earth that what changes must have a changer, and that changer must be capable of perfection, and that He can send messengers. If He sends a messenger and shows the truth of his message by a single miracle, no one has an excuse. These are the ones who remember Allah in every state. And Allah knows best.

**Question 8:** The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And they reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾. We have already explained the meaning of "they remember," which is either remembrance by the tongue or prayer, obligatory and optional. Thus Allah joined another act of worship to one of them (in some manuscripts: "joined another worship, which is reflection"), namely reflection on the power of Allah and His creatures, and the lessons He scattered, so that this may increase their insight:

*And in everything there is a sign*
*indicating that He is one.*

Al-Qurtubi said: It has been said that "yatafakkarun" (they reflect) is coordinated (ʿatf) with the circumstantial clause (al-ḥāl). It has also been said that it is an independent clause (munqaṭiʿ), but the first view is closer to the meaning. Al-fikra (reflection) is the heart's repeated turning over of a matter. One says "tafakkara" (he reflected), and a man who is "fakīr" is one who reflects much. The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by a people who were reflecting about Allah, and he said: "Reflect on the creation, and do not reflect on the Creator, for you cannot measure His measure." Reflection, consideration, and the expansion of the mind over created things are what is meant, as He said: ﴿And they reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth.﴾

It is related that Sufyan al-Thawri (may Allah be pleased with him) prayed two rak'ahs behind the Maqam (the Station of Ibrahim). Then he raised his head to the sky, and when he saw the stars he fainted. He used to urinate blood because of his prolonged grief and reflection.
